'''Ōshikōchi no Ajihari''' ({{lang|ja|大河内 味張}}, also {{lang|ja|凡河内味張}}; dates of birth and death unknown) was a {{ill|Gōzoku|ja|豪族|lt=regional magnate|lt_ja=豪族}} of early sixth-century Japan and one of the '''{{ill|Ōshikōchi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|ja|凡河内国造|lt=Ōshikōchi no Kuni no Miyatsuko|lt_ja=凡河内国造}}'''. His {{ill|Kabane|ja|カバネ|lt=kabane|lt_ja=姓}} was {{ill|Atai (kabane)|ja|直 (姓)|lt=atai|lt_ja=直}}. He was also called '''Kurohi''' ({{lang|ja|黒梭}}).

== Career ==
The Ōshikōchi clan ({{ill|Ōshikōchi clan|ja|凡河内氏|lt=Ōshikōchi clan|lt_ja=凡河内氏}}) claimed descent from {{ill|Amatsuhikone|ja|天津彦根命|lt=Amatsuhikone|lt_ja=天津彦根命}}, who was born when {{ill|Amaterasu|ja|天照大神|lt=Amaterasu|lt_ja=天照大神}} and {{ill|Susanoo|ja|素戔嗚尊|lt=Susanoo|lt_ja=素戔嗚尊}} made their {{ill|Ukehi|ja|うけい|lt=pledge|lt_ja=誓約}}, and was the family of the Ōshikōchi no Kuni no Miyatsuko. {{ill|Ōshikōchi no Kagatsu|ja|凡河内香賜|lt=Ōshikōchi no Kagatsu|lt_ja=凡河内香賜}}, who in the ninth year of {{ill|Emperor Yūryaku|ja|雄略天皇|lt=Emperor Yūryaku|lt_ja=雄略天皇}} violated and killed a court attendant (''uneme'') at the Munakata shrine, belonged to Ajihari's family. That Kagatsu was caught and killed at Aihara in {{ill|Mishima District, Osaka|ja|三島郡 (大阪府)|lt=Mishima District|lt_ja=三島郡}} is thought to be closely connected with the events below.

In the seventh month of the first year of {{ill|Emperor Ankan|ja|安閑天皇|lt=Emperor Ankan|lt_ja=安閑天皇}} (estimated {{ill|534|ja|534年|lt=534|lt_ja=534年}}), the emperor, wishing to spread his empress's name through the land, decided to set up a {{ill|Miyake|ja|屯倉|lt=miyake|lt_ja=屯倉}} (royal estate) bearing it, and sent an envoy to look for good rice land. Ajihari, grudging the loss of his fields, answered:

"In a drought this land is hard to water, and when there is even a little overflow it floods easily. The labour is very great and the harvest very small."

The envoy believed him and went home.<ref>''Nihon Shoki'', book 18, Ankan 2, seventh month, first day.</ref>

In the intercalary twelfth month of that year, however, the emperor suddenly travelled with {{ill|Ōtomo no Kanamura|ja|大伴金村|lt=Ōtomo no Kanamura|lt_ja=大伴金村}} to {{ill|Mishima District, Osaka|ja|三島郡 (大阪府)|lt=Mishima|lt_ja=三嶋}}, the home ground of the Ōshikōchi clan, and asked the ''agata-nushi'' {{ill|Mishima no Iibo|ja|三嶋飯粒|lt=Iibo|lt_ja=飯粒}} about good land. Iibo willingly offered the emperor forty ''chō'' of land at {{ill|Takafu Miyake|ja|竹村屯倉|lt=Takafu|lt_ja=竹村}}. Ajihari's lie was exposed by this, and he was told that he must no longer serve as district governor ({{ill|Kuni no miyatsuko|ja|国造|lt=kuni no miyatsuko|lt_ja=国造}}). Ajihari, prostrate with fear and in a cold sweat, said:

"My crime deserves ten thousand deaths. From now on I will present to the emperor five hundred hoe-labourers (''kuwa-yohoro'') in spring and five hundred in autumn, without fail for all my descendants. With this I beg pardon, and let it be a warning for later generations."

He is also said to have given Ōtomo no Kanamura six ''chō'' of the Saita fields in {{ill|Kawachi Province|ja|河内国|lt=Kawachi|lt_ja=河内}}. In this way, it is said, the {{ill|Kakibe|ja|部曲|lt=kakibe|lt_ja=部曲}} of the Kawachi district first became {{ill|Tabe|ja|田部|lt=tabe|lt_ja=田部}} (royal estate cultivators).<ref>''Nihon Shoki'', book 18, Ankan 2, intercalary twelfth month, fourth day.</ref>

{{ill|Akihito Hirabayashi|ja|平林章仁|lt=Hirabayashi Akihito|lt_ja=平林章仁}} describes this as an incident produced by the setting up of royal estates, and probably the result of a policy that sought at once to guarantee that Ankan's father {{ill|Emperor Keitai|ja|継体天皇|lt=Emperor Keitai|lt_ja=継体天皇}} was the rightful successor of the earlier royal line descended from {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|lt=Emperor Nintoku|lt_ja=仁徳天皇}}, and to secure the economic base of the kingship.

The Ōshikōchi no Atai family received the {{ill|Kabane|ja|カバネ|lt=kabane|lt_ja=姓}} of {{ill|Muraji|ja|連|lt=muraji|lt_ja=連}} in the twelfth year of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|天武天皇|lt=Emperor Tenmu|lt_ja=天武天皇}} ({{ill|683|ja|683年|lt=683|lt_ja=683年}})<ref>''Nihon Shoki'', book 29, Tenmu 12, ninth month, 23rd day.</ref> and that of {{ill|Imiki|ja|忌寸|lt=imiki|lt_ja=忌寸}} in Tenmu 14 ({{ill|685|ja|685年|lt=685|lt_ja=685年}}).<ref>''Nihon Shoki'', book 29, Tenmu 14, sixth month, 20th day.</ref>
